Tolls at the Colombia Solidarity International Bridge are now half what they were. Nuevo León cut the fees by 50%, a move aimed at attracting more cross-border business through South Texas and strengthening trade ties between Mexico and the United States, according to KGNS.

Leaders expect the lower fees to reduce shipping costs and direct more commercial traffic into Laredo, which already handles a large share of U.S.-Mexico overland trade through its international bridges. The Colombia bridge, west of Laredo in Anáhuac, Nuevo León, is the crossing most closely tied to the Colombia–Laredo corridor and its industrial parks.

Laredo Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño met at the bridge with the governors of Nuevo León and Jalisco around the announcement, according to KGNS. The report did not state a specific effective date for the cut, presenting it as already in place.

The toll cut lands days before the November 3 election and alongside a $200 million expansion announced earlier in October for the Colombia–Laredo International Bridge, a project local officials have pitched as a way to grow the region's trade capacity.

What to watch next: whether truck traffic through the Colombia crossing rises in the coming weeks, and whether the lower tolls translate into measurable savings for shippers moving freight through Laredo.

Sources:

  • KGNS, "Nuevo León cuts toll fees 50% at Colombia Solidarity International Bridge," October 29, 2026
  • Laredo Morning Times, "Nuevo León cuts toll charges 50% on route to Colombia crossing," October 29, 2026
